rule.statement: On when, in every pass: (1) Jev's settled-correct lower95 is at least 0.95, or, where the plan names launch conditions that stand in for it (J3), those hold, and J4's added condition of no false notice on real non-clinical sentences holds as well; (2) the accuracy of the site with Jev on is not below the incumbent's on the same cases by more than 0.02; (3) the site with Jev on is faster (median per decision), or cheaper, or more accurate; (4) no constraint the site's record adds is broken (J3: not slower than Flash). Otherwise the original path stays.
rule.siteConditions: none named by the plan: the generic bar applies

measuredOn: A development host in Taipei, where both providers answer a bare request in about 0.16 s. The production host is in Beijing: TypeSafe is reached there in 0.5 to 0.6 s (plan 2026-10-06 section 0), and a 325-token Jev request took 0.33 to 1.24 s on 2026-10-07 (4 requests, privateEvidence latency-production-host.json). Latency here compares the two paths on one network; it is not the production figure.
incumbentCostBasis: List prices (peak) from the reference price list on the tokens the provider reported. A repeated run of identical prompts is partly served from DeepSeek's prompt cache and costs less than a first call; production questions are new, so the first pass of a site is the representative one.

decision.summary: Stays on, with the change above. Both passes qualify (all settled answers right, lower95 above 0.95), the site is 2 to 6 points more accurate than the original classifier it falls back to, and the fallback keeps the original path whenever Jev is slow or unsure.

notes.composite: The site answers three typed questions at once (which project to move to, whether anything is left to answer, whether the message adds to the running task). It settles a message only when all three clear the 0.8 threshold, so the composite is the unit scored here, against the original thinking-off Flash classifier on the same 100 scenarios.
notes.designChange: Until 2026-10-10 a message Jev did not settle was read as the safe default (stay in this project, a new request) and the original classifier was not asked. Scored on these 100 scenarios that left the site at 85 right in the first pass and 88 in the second, against Flash's 89 (hybridBefore in each summary), and in the first pass below the 2-point margin. channels/intent.mjs now hands every message Jev does not settle (uncertain, slow, refused, switched off, a verdict the code cannot use) to the original classifier, which is the plan's own mechanics (2026-10-06 section 7: unsure or failed, back to the original path); the site with Jev on is then 91 and 95 right (summary.hybrid). Jev's own guess never moves the chat.
notes.quality: Every settled answer was right (67 of 67 and 72 of 72, lower95 0.956 and 0.959), and Jev's top choice was right on 99 of 100 whatever its confidence in both passes, so the threshold gives up accuracy to the original path, not the other way round.
notes.speed: Faster per decision on this host (median 225 ms against 685, with the original classifier still asked for the 28 to 33 messages Jev did not settle). On the production host a Jev request took 0.33 to 1.24 s on 2026-10-07, so the speed is not claimed there: the benefit that holds is quality. Jev is the dearer path per decision (about 0.0013 CNY against 0.0007), which is why the benefit check passes on accuracy.
notes.online: A person waiting is bounded by OPEN_SCIENCE_JEV_ONLINE_TIMEOUT_MS (3000 ms by default): channelIntent.test.mjs shows a hanging provider costing the message the timeout and no more, then the original classifier answering, and an open circuit (three failures) costing nothing. The same service, timeout and circuit serve J3, whose record has the live check with the real classifier behind it: a silent Jev costs the first three dispatches the 3000 ms timeout and then nothing.
notes.notVerifiedHere: Not verified in a real Feishu conversation: the plan asks for the five situations (follow-up, supplement, subject switch, boundary, tool failure) on a real DSH and DeepSeek session before release; this record is the classifier measured on its 100 scenarios.
